info.name: Citizens Online
info.summary: Run online citizens' assemblies in Nextcloud Talk breakout rooms
info.description:
Citizens Online runs **online deliberative assemblies** on top of Nextcloud Talk. An organizer defines a session with rounds and questions; the app creates the Talk conversation, splits participants into breakout rooms, keeps time, facilitates the discussion through a bot, and turns what was said into a reviewed report.
## How it works
1. Create a session, add Nextcloud users as participants, define one or more rounds. 2. Assign participants to rooms — manually or randomly. 3. Start a round: the app creates Talk breakout rooms, moves everyone into theirs, and starts the clock. 4. Each participant's browser records their own microphone, so every transcript line carries a real name rather than an anonymous speaker label. 5. A facilitator bot watches speaking time and the clock and posts into each room. 6. When the round ends, the app analyses each room's discussion, clusters findings across rooms, and an organizer reviews everything before it becomes a report.
## Data processing — please read
* **Audio** is captured in the participant's browser and stored on your server. It is sent to a speech-to-text engine only if an administrator configures one. With a self-hosted Vosk or Whisper server, recordings never leave your infrastructure. * **Transcript text** (never audio) is sent to the analysis endpoint an administrator configures. That can be your own server. * Nothing is sent anywhere until an administrator sets it up. Participants see exactly which engines are in use before they consent.
## Ethical AI Rating
Green when transcription and analysis run against self-hosted endpoints; orange when a hosted provider is configured. The choice is the administrator's and is disclosed to participants.
## Status
Alpha. The pipeline runs end to end, but this is early software: bring your own privacy notice and deletion practice before running a real assembly.
